172.transcription: Remove all Pursuit and Checkpoint tokens from the board.
172.flavor: The target slipped through the network, safely into Soviet territory. He is a gardening contractor that deals in plants, seeds, and so on. It is unclear what he was carrying, but it looks like he's sending another shipment this month.

173.flavor: Despite your best efforts, your teams couldn't bug the control center.

174.transcription: Open Door 46. Then open Door F and place that rule in the rulebook. Then draw the Pause card in the Legacy deck and read the back of it.
174.flavor: The Soviets proved easy to locate, as if they weren't expecting opposition. Your teams made a quick sweep and prevented the experiment from taking place. Quick analysis suggests that the Soviets were holding the trials around city parks.

175.transcription: DESTROY the Infection card of the city where you quarantined the population. Remove (or cross out) the Exposed City sticker near that city. It is no longer an Exposed City.
175.flavor: Your team quarantined the population of the city to contain the problem. The local government has created a plausible cover story that should buy time.

176.transcription: Place a Bug sticker on the corner of the Control Center sticker in South America to show that it was bugged.
176.flavor: The bug was successfully planted. So far, you've heard nondescript chatter about a Siberian compound, but nothing actionable.

177.transcription: If you failed the objective "Bug the Control Center," destroy it and find card 88 in the Operations deck. Use this objective as your third objective for the second half of May. If you succeeded with that objective, mark it as complete at the start of the next game (as normal).
177.flavor: "We must do better than this. If we allow ourselves to fall too far behind the Soviets, we risk losing everything."

178.transcription: Turn each city where the trial was NOT disrupted into an Exposed City (following the rules for Marking Exposed Cities). Place these Infection cards in the Game End area and destroy any unused Infection cards. Then move all three City cards under the Disrupt Trial objective to the Player discard pile. Then draw the Pause card in the Legacy deck and read it.
178.flavor: This MEDUSA strain is highly virulent. The cities are already having issues. The press has taken notice, and preventing outbreaks at home will be challenging.

179.transcription: Remove all Pursuit and Checkpoint tokens from the board.
179.flavor: Cooper is missing once again, and you suspect he won't be found. Of Sabik, there is no further news. He has disappeared into hiding, but you receive a message. It reads, "I have a few other things to take care of, but don't worry. I haven't forgotten about you."

180.transcription: If the objective "Hunt Down Soviet Exporter" is incomplete, you may immediately place 1 Checkpoint token on the board. Return the player pawn in the PEARL Compound to Novosibirsk. Players may still Infiltrate PEARL if they wish.
180.flavor:
There is no cure. All you find are records of empty promises from PEARL scientists to the Kremlin about viable treatment before December: no data, no samples, no progress.

The Soviets will not be able to insulate themselves from the plague. The scientists are hiding their failure while the world hangs in the balance. If the Soviets launch the fully-weaponized MEDUSA plague, there will be no cure. For anyone.

181.transcription:
If you attempt to forcefully stop Sabik, read entry 144.

If you attempt to talk Sabik out of killing Cooper, read entry 164.
181.flavor: You arrive at the scene. Cooper is incoherent, drugged, and barely standing. Wounded in the pursuit, the cornered Sabik clutches a syringe in one hand and Cooper's collar in the other. His wild, ghastly eyes dart back and forth. "You have to listen to me. I was set up! The CIA had him this whole time. They told you I killed him so that you wouldn't trust me! They betrayed me. They'll betray you too!" He gestures wildly with the syringe. Blood pulses through veins along the translucent skin of his temples. "Look at me! LOOK WHAT THEY DID TO ME!" he screams, bringing the syringe towards Cooper's neck.

182.transcription: Return the player pawn in the PEARL Compound to Novosibirsk. Players may still infiltrate PEARL Compound.
182.flavor:
August 10, 1961. Testing of Chuma 0 - Diplulmaris Antarctica (C0dA). Subject Alpha: Sabik. American. Early test of the Diplulmaris Antarctica collagen gene to evaluate weakening the vasculature in mammals: making the skin translucent.

Day 1, trial 1. 45cc C0dA at 0300. Violent seizures. Slight transparentization of dermis from genome, as hoped, and severe fever. Note: Restrain subject in future trials.

Day 10, trial 2. 75cc C0dA at 0430. Further seizures, but subject restrained. Additional transparentization, revealing viscera, muscular systems, and arteries, in particular near eyes, mouth, back of hands. Emotional extremes in subject, including periods of lethargy and violent outbursts. Note: C0dA virus must pass the blood-brain barrier to effect aggression and seizures.

Day 30, trial 3. 200cc C0dA at 0415. Physical reaction led to cardiac arrest. Subject revived and stabilized. Near complete transparentization of dermis. Editorial note: Subject features the "sufficiently horrific appearance" requested by the KGB. A population suffering from its effects would surely experience significant unrest.

Day 40, further trials suspended. C0dA ineffective at low dosage, and insufficient supply for the necessary higher dosage. Decades of testing and refinement will be required to weaponize it. Proceed with pathogen retrieved from Lake Baikal for PROJEKT MEDUSA.

183.transcription: Put the Infiltration cards for Sabik's Safehouse into the reserve. No further information.
183.flavor: Sabik or one of his loyal operatives noticed your monitoring. Photographs of your team were taped to the exterior windows with your real names written on them. A warning: he knows who you are.

184.transcription:
If you allow him to proceed, read entry 138.

If you attempt to forcefully stop Sabik, read entry 158.
184.flavor:
After your team extracts Cooper, you bring him to Sabik. "Coop...I always wondered what I'd say to you if we crossed paths. What you did to me...it's unforgivable." Cooper pleads, terrified, as Sabik leans close, veins pulsing beneath translucent flesh.

Sabik frowns. "You know what? It's not enough to see it, is it? You need to understand. You need to REALLY UNDERSTAND!" Sabik walks to the nearby workbench, tearing open medical supplies. Moments later, he empties a vial into a large syringe. "This is C0dA." His voice is calm now, his hand steady as he walks toward Cooper. "This is what you did to me."

185.flavor: The teams could not quarantine the city.

186.transcription: Place a Control Center sticker on the target city. Place a Bug sticker over the corner of the Control Center sticker to show that it was bugged. Take the target City card under the objective and add it to the hand of the player who completed this objective.
186.flavor: While bugging the control center, the team found an encrypted note in the trash. "?????? launched on schedule. Wind and ???? tracked. ???? gathered for Operation LION'S TOOTH."

187.transcription: Place a Bug sticker on the corner of the Control Center sticker in Asia to show that it was bugged.
187.flavor: Posing as electricians, your team infiltrated the control center and planted the bug. Monitoring data for the facility is already routing back to Langley.

188.transcription: Take 1 Action token and give it to one player. Remove all Checkpoint tokens from the board.
188.flavor: The Soviets have grafted the final, deadly strain of the MEDUSA plague onto ragweed pollen, inspired by the Japanese Fu-Go balloon bombs from World War II. Next month, they intend to launch Operation LION'S TOOTH, a series of weather balloons loaded with millions of grains of contaminated pollen. Once the balloons reach their targets, they will release the pollen, and there will be nowhere to hide.
